sentences.text: The largest known specimens of Iniopteryx measure between 30 and 35 centimeters in length, and their internal skeleton was composed of calcified cartilage.

This fish possessed large eyes positioned behind the nasal openings, supported by sclerotic rings made of calcified cartilage, and small, hook-shaped denticles in its mouth that may have been composed of orthodentine.

Male Iniopteryx had a large, recurved denticle on their pelvic fin that functioned as a tenaculum, similar to those found in chimaeras, and the animal was characterized by having fins similar to those of flying fish.
Researchers suggest that Iniopteryx had small, fragile teeth that limited its diet to soft food.
Males possessed a unique, recurved denticle on their pelvic fin that functioned as a tenaculum, a structure similar to those found in chimaeras.
The animal was characterized by having fins similar to those of flying fish.
The geological sites where fossils were found are considered Konservat-Lagerstätten, meaning the fossils are exceptionally well preserved.
Iniopteryx lacked vertebral centra and had an entirely uncalcified notochord, unlike modern chimaeras which have calcified rings.

The large, nape-positioned pectoral fins were likely the primary means of locomotion for Iniopteryx, and researchers compared the movement of these fins to the flight stroke of a bird or the forelimbs of a sea turtle.
Fossil evidence from stomach infills in specimens PF6672 and PF6646 shows that Iniopteryx ate arthropod exoskeletons, conodonts, and plant matter.
Researchers theorize that the low number of female fossils compared to males was caused by higher predation on females, while males used their denticle-covered pectoral fins for defense.
Iniopteryx is classified within the class Chondrichthyes and belongs to the order Iniopterygia, with the parent group being the family Iniopterygidae.
Iniopteryx is the type genus of the Iniopterygiformes, a group of cartilaginous fish debated as either stem-holocephalans or stem-group chondrichthyans related to Elasmobranchii and Holocephali.

Fossils of Iniopteryx have been found in the U.S. states of Nebraska and Indiana, but they have been found abundantly only in Pennsylvania, North America, with 14 recorded fossil occurrences in the Paleobiology Database.
It is hypothesized that Iniopteryx and related iniopterygians were visitors to basin environments rather than permanent residents.
It is debated whether Iniopteryx had a holostylic jaw suspension, as later research contradicted the original description that claimed the upper jaws were fused to the braincase.
